title: $64,428 Salary: You Keep $53,948. Where Does the Rest Go? #shorts
description:
The typical full-time worker earns $1,239 a week (BLS median, Q3 2026): $64,428 a year. Paid every two weeks, that's $2,478. Social Security takes 6.2% ($154), Medicare 1.45% ($36) and federal income tax about $213, so take-home is about $2,075, before state tax in most states. Over a year: $53,948 kept. The surprise: this worker is in the 12% bracket but pays just 8.6% of their pay in income tax, because the first $16,100 (the standard deduction) isn't taxed and the next $12,400 of taxable income is taxed at 10%. And the employer pays another 7.65% ($4,929 a year) on top, so the job costs about $69,357.

Math: single filer, 2026 federal tax brackets and standard deduction (IRS, Rev. Proc. 2025-32), no other deductions or credits; Social Security 6.2% (2026 wage base $184,500, SSA) and Medicare 1.45%, matched by the employer. State and local taxes, health insurance and retirement contributions are not included. Pay: BLS median usual weekly earnings of full-time wage and salary workers (FRED LES1252881500Q), Q3 2026, x 52.
